chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a free woman who married a slave under the assumption that he was free, but later learned that he was a slave. He said: 'She has the choice; if she wishes, she can remain with him, and if she wishes, she can leave. If he has consummated the marriage with her, she is entitled to the dowry; and if he has not consummated it with her, she is entitled to nothing. And if he consummated the marriage with her after she knew he was a slave and she accepted that, then he has the choice regarding her.'
Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'If he married her under the assumption that he was sane, and sanity issues became apparent to her regarding him, she has the choice.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a free woman who marries a slave if she discovers his status after marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *ta'dil* (concealment of defects) in marriage, granting the free woman the option (*khiyar*) to annul the contract upon discovering the slave status. It distinguishes between financial rights, such as the dowry (*mahr*) which is contingent on consummation, and the right of choice, which remains with the woman even if the defect is insanity (*jinnah*), reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on informed consent in marital contracts.
